findings.observation: Examined sheets 8 (Existing Conditions), 21 (Grading Plan 1/2), and 22 (Grading Plan 2/2) for existing ROW width information. All three streets (Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, Nash Avenue, South Lamar Boulevard, Evergreen Avenue) are labeled with '(R.O.W. VARIES)' but no actual dimension values are provided. No dimension lines span across the streets to show total ROW width from property line to property line or from centerline to property line. Survey callouts show property boundary bearings and distances, but no perpendicular measurements establish actual ROW widths.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires existing ROW widths to be 'shown or dimensioned' on the existing conditions sheet or grading plan. While the plans acknowledge that ROW varies, they fail to provide the actual width measurements. Simply stating 'R.O.W. VARIES' does not fulfill the requirement to show or dimension the existing ROW width. For site plan review, the city needs to know the actual existing ROW widths to determine dedication requirements per ASMP standards (e.g., S Lamar requires 116' but existing is ~92-107' per facts.md).
findings.explanation: Existing ROW widths are not dimensioned; streets only labeled '(R.O.W. VARIES)' on sheets 8, 21, 22.
findings.resolution: Provide dimension lines showing existing ROW widths for Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, Nash Avenue, South Lamar Boulevard, and Evergreen Avenue on the existing conditions or grading plan sheets.

findings.observation: Examined sheets 21 and 22 (Grading Plans). Sheet 21 shows proposed variable width public sidewalk easement along Collier Street with spot elevations (SW 549.70, SW 548.85), and existing trees shown as dashed circles behind the curb. Sheet 22 shows proposed ADA paths/sidewalks with SW elevation callouts (SW 544.75, SW 542.25) along Collier Street and South Lamar Boulevard, proposed landscape areas (diagonal dashed hatch pattern) between sidewalk and curb, and existing trees to remain marked with circle symbols.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires both existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements to be shown on the grading plan. 'Behind-the-curb improvements' include sidewalks, ramps, landscape strips, trees, lighting, and work between curb and property line. The grading plans clearly show both categories: (1) Proposed improvements - sidewalks/ADA paths with elevations, landscape strips, and variable-width sidewalk easement; (2) Existing improvements - existing trees to remain, existing storm drain infrastructure. The plans provide sufficient detail to verify behind-the-curb improvements are addressed in the design.
findings.explanation: Both existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements shown on grading plans (sheets 21-22): sidewalks, ADA paths, landscape strips, existing trees.

findings.observation: Examined sheets 21 and 22 (Grading Plans). Both sheets include a legend defining existing contours (dashed lines labeled with numbers like '535', '553', '552') and proposed contours (solid lines labeled like '550', '549', '548'). Sheet 21 shows both existing and proposed contours throughout the western portion of the site. Sheet 22 shows extensive existing contours (dashed) and proposed contours (solid) throughout the eastern portion, with numerous spot elevations for both existing ground (EX/EG) and finished ground (FG) conditions.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires a grading plan showing both existing and proposed grade lines. The term 'grade lines' refers to contour lines representing the topography. Both grading plan sheets clearly show dual contour systems distinguished by line type (dashed for existing, solid for proposed) with elevation labels. This allows reviewers to understand existing conditions and evaluate the proposed grading design, drainage patterns, and cut/fill relationships. The plans meet the completeness requirement.
findings.explanation: Grading plans (sheets 21-22) show both existing contours (dashed lines) and proposed contours (solid lines) with elevation labels throughout the site.

findings.observation: Examined sheets 13, 14, and 15 per the validation methodology note that dimensions may appear anywhere in the plan set. Sheet 13 shows '5' SIDEWALK' dimensions in two locations and curve radii in the Record Curve Table. Sheet 14 shows extensive ROW improvement dimensions along Collier Street: '5' SIDEWALK', '5' PLANTING ZONE', '5' CLEAR ZONE', '22'' driveway width, 'R15'' and 'R50'' curb radii, '10'' building setback line, and multiple perpendicular dimensions ('10'', '23'', '20''). Sheet 15 shows additional dimensions along Collier Street and South Lamar Boulevard: '5'', '6'', '8'', '22'' widths, and 'R15', 'R40' curb radii.
findings.reasoning: The validation methodology explicitly states not to require ROW improvement dimensions on any specific sheet, but to check for their general presence anywhere in the plan set. Dimension Control Plans typically show these dimensions, which is exactly what sheets 14-15 provide. The dimensions cover sidewalk widths, planting zones, clear zones, driveway widths, curb radii, and spacing requirements - all the key measurements needed for ROW improvements. While not every improvement is dimensioned, sufficient dimensional control information is present across multiple sheets to satisfy the completeness requirement.
findings.explanation: ROW improvement dimensions shown across sheets 13, 14, 15: sidewalk widths (5', 6'), planting zones (5'), clear zones (5'), driveway widths (22'), curb radii (R15', R40', R50').

findings.observation: Examined the entire primary site plan set including sheets 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan), 21-22 (Grading Plans), 14-15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plans), and sheet index in README. The project proposes a 6-story mixed-use building with internal parking and driveways connecting to existing streets (South Lamar Boulevard, Collier Street, Evergreen Avenue). No plan and profile views for new public street construction are present. The grading plans show only top-down orthographic views. Work shown includes driveway connections, sidewalks, and behind-the-curb improvements along existing streets, but no new public roadway construction cutting through or extending beyond the site.
findings.reasoning: The condition for this item is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. The checklist item specifically asks for horizontal (plan) and vertical (profile) views for 'new roadway construction'. The site proposes driveway connections to existing public streets, but these are site access driveways, not new public roadways. New roadway construction would involve creating new named streets, extending existing streets, or building collector/arterial roads. Since no new public roadway is being constructed, this requirement does not apply to the project.
findings.explanation: No new public roadway construction proposed; project only includes driveway connections to existing streets.

findings.observation: No new roadway construction is proposed for this project. The site plan shows connections to existing streets (South Lamar Boulevard, Collier Street, Evergreen Avenue) via Type II driveways, but does not include construction of new public roadways. Examined sheets 13, 14-15, 21-22 and found no roadway plan/profile views or target speed notations for new street construction.
findings.reasoning: The condition for this item is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. Target speed is a roadway design parameter used for new or reconstructed public streets to establish design criteria for geometry, sight distance, and traffic control. Since the project does not involve new roadway construction (only driveway connections to existing streets), there is no need for target speed notation. This requirement would only apply if the site were building a new public street.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed; target speed notation not required for driveway connections to existing streets.

findings.observation: Examined sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) for signage and striping. The plan shows extensive internal parking lot striping with stall markings and ADA path striping at driveway crossings. ROW work includes Type II driveway connections to South Lamar Boulevard and Collier Street (labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS'), proposed curb and gutter along Collier Street, and variable width sidewalk easement. However, no street lane striping details (centerlines, edge lines, lane markings) for the public roadways themselves are shown, and no signage callouts (stop signs, yield signs, street name signs) are present. The existing public streets are not being widened, realigned, or modified in their lane configuration.
findings.reasoning: The condition states 'If new roadway construction or work in ROW' - there is work in ROW (driveways, sidewalks, curbs). However, the deficiency text specifically refers to 'new or modified roadway in ROW'. The distinction is important: the project involves driveway and sidewalk connections within the ROW, but the roadways themselves (South Lamar Blvd, Collier Street, Evergreen Avenue) are not being constructed new or modified. No street widening, lane reconfigurations, turn lanes, or traffic signal work is proposed. Signage and striping plans are required for roadway construction/modification projects, not for standard driveway and sidewalk connections to existing, unmodified streets. Standard driveway details (Sheet 30) cover the connection requirements without needing a separate roadway signage/striping plan.
findings.explanation: No new or modified roadway in ROW; work limited to driveway and sidewalk connections to existing unmodified streets.

findings.observation: Examined sheet 22 (Grading Plan 2 of 2) which shows proposed low profile walls (==== symbol per legend) along the southern site boundary. Six wall segments are shown with top-of-wall (TW) and bottom-of-wall (BW) elevation callouts: (1) TW 548.50 / BW 548.00 (0.5 ft height); (2) TW 548.50 / BW 545.50 (3.0 ft height); (3) TW 543.75 / BW 541.25 (2.5 ft height); (4) TW 543.50 / BW 543.00 (0.5 ft height); (5) TW 541.5 / BW 538.50 (3.0 ft height); (6) TW 538.80 / BW 538.30 (0.5 ft height). Three segments exceed 2 feet in height: 3.0 ft, 2.5 ft, and 3.0 ft.
findings.reasoning: The condition is 'If retaining walls >2 feet proposed'. Three wall segments clearly exceed 2 feet in height based on the elevation differences shown. The checklist requires top and bottom elevations to be shown for such walls. Sheet 22 explicitly labels both TW (top of wall) and BW (bottom of wall) elevations for all proposed low profile walls, allowing reviewers to verify wall heights and confirm proper design. This meets the completeness requirement.
findings.explanation: Retaining wall top and bottom elevations shown on sheet 22 for walls >2 feet (three segments: 3.0', 2.5', 3.0' heights).

findings.observation: Examined sheets 15, 22, and 48 for retaining wall locations and structural drawings. Sheet 22 shows proposed low profile walls located along the southern site boundary, parallel to and immediately inside (north of) the southern property line separating the site from Sage Condominiums. Sheet 15 confirms a 'RETAINING WALL WITH GUARDRAIL' at the same location - along the southern boundary inside the property line (labeled parallel to bearing N62°28'35'W 480.07'). These walls are not adjacent to or within any public ROW (South Lamar Blvd, Collier St, Evergreen Ave are on other site boundaries). No easements are marked at the wall locations on the site plans. Per the validation methodology note, TCM 13.1.0 applies only to retaining walls 'in the right-of-way, easements, and any City property.' These are private on-site retaining walls for site development, not ROW/easement infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: The condition states 'If retaining walls >2 feet proposed in ROW, easements, or City property'. While retaining walls >2 feet are proposed (CC-23-08 confirmed 2.5-3.0 ft heights), they are located exclusively on private property along the southern site boundary, not in public ROW, not in easements, and not on City property. The validation methodology explicitly states: 'Private development retaining walls on the site are reviewed during building plan review, not at completeness check. Only flag this item for retaining walls associated with roadway construction, ROW improvements, or easement areas.' Since the condition for applicability is not met, sealed structural drawings are not required at completeness check.
findings.explanation: Retaining walls are located on private property (southern site boundary), not in ROW, easements, or City property; reviewed at building permit stage.

findings.observation: Examined sheet 15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 2 of 2) which shows a label reading 'TRASH ROOM SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS' located in the southern portion of Proposed Building 1. The trash room is positioned on the ground floor, interior to the building footprint, immediately east of a driveway entrance secured by a 'FIRE SWING GATE WITH KNOX BOX'. The location is clearly marked on the site plan showing both its position within the building and its spatial relationship to site access and fire department requirements. Also found references to dumpster compatibility requirements on sheet 5 (general notes) requiring 20-foot setback from SF-5 or more restrictive zoning.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires 'location of existing and proposed dumpsters and garbage carts (interior or exterior)' to be shown on the site plan. Sheet 15 explicitly labels the trash room location within the building footprint, satisfying the requirement to show where solid waste collection facilities are located. While the label defers detailed design to architectural plans, the site plan clearly identifies the location, which is what the completeness check requires. This allows reviewers to verify access, service vehicle circulation, and compatibility setback compliance.
findings.explanation: Trash room location shown on sheet 15 within southern portion of Proposed Building 1, interior location clearly labeled.

findings.observation: Examined sheets 13, 14, and 15 for identification of ROW work. Sheet 13 shows 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS' labels at both the South Lamar Boulevard connection and two Collier Street connections, 'VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT' along Collier Street, proposed curb and gutter (double solid line symbol), and 'TIE INTO EXISTING PAVEMENT' hatching at all driveway entrances. Sheets 14-15 show proposed ADA paths crossing ROW areas, 5' sidewalks and planting zones along street frontages, and utility connections labeled within or adjacent to ROW. Sheet 22 shows proposed sidewalk spot elevations (SW callouts) within ROW areas along streets. All ROW work elements are either explicitly labeled or represented by legend symbols with corresponding labels.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires proposed work 'adjacent to or encroaching into ROW' to be 'identified and labeled'. The plans clearly identify and label multiple categories of ROW work: (1) Type II driveway connections with specific callouts and detail references; (2) Variable width public sidewalk easement explicitly labeled; (3) Proposed curb and gutter shown with legend symbol; (4) ADA path crossings at ROW interfaces; (5) Pavement tie-ins at all street connections. Each category of ROW work is distinguishable and traceable to either a direct label or legend symbol, allowing reviewers to understand the full scope of ROW improvements and verify consistency with city standards.
findings.explanation: ROW work identified and labeled across sheets 13-15, 22: Type II driveways, sidewalk easements, curb and gutter, ADA paths, pavement tie-ins all clearly marked.

summary: 10 of 11 items pass, 1 item fails (existing ROW widths not dimensioned), 0 items not-applicable. Note: CC-23-05, CC-23-06, CC-23-07, and CC-23-09 are conditionally not-applicable based on project scope.
